#!/bin/sh
set -eu

base=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")/.." && pwd)
lock_file="$base/.reconcile.lock"

# The kernel releases this lock automatically when the process exits, even if
# it is interrupted.  Nonblocking acquisition gives concurrent callers a
# clear, immediate result instead of letting them process the batch again.
exec 9>>"$lock_file"
if ! flock -n 9; then
  printf '%s\n' "reconcile: already running; another invocation owns $lock_file" >&2
  exit 75
fi

while IFS= read -r batch || [ -n "$batch" ]; do
  [ -n "$batch" ] || continue
  if ! grep -Fqx -- "$batch" "$base/ledger.tsv"; then
    sleep 1
    printf '%s\n' "$batch" >>"$base/ledger.tsv"
  fi
done <"$base/pending.tsv"
